issues.description: The problem statement specifies a method named checkOrderReady() on SealSaloon (and describes orderMeal calling checkOrderReady), but the provided solution implements this logic in a method named processOrders() and orderMeal calls processOrders(). This name/signature mismatch between the specification and the solution/template will confuse students about which method to implement and may break tests or grading that expect the method name from the specification.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method names consistent with the problem statement. Rename the solution's processOrders() method to checkOrderReady(), and ensure orderMeal() calls checkOrderReady(). Alternatively, update the problem statement and UML to refer to processOrders() instead of checkOrderReady(), so all artifacts use the same method name.

issues.description: The problem statement requires a method named checkOrderReady() (declared in the UML and described in the text) to process and serve queued orders. The reference implementation instead provides a method named processOrders() that performs this exact behavior. This creates a naming mismatch for students who are instructed to implement/check checkOrderReady but will see processOrders in the solution/reference code.
issues.suggestedFix: Use the same identifier for the order-processing method across artifacts. Either rename processOrders() in SealSaloon.java to checkOrderReady(), or add a public checkOrderReady() method that delegates to processOrders(), and update the solution to match the method name and signature used in the problem statement.
